 Kyrie Irving (knee) is out for Sunday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Initially questionable, Irving is out after playing 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers. His absence frees up minutes and opportunities for Walter Clayton Jr. and Marcus Sasser, even if neither of them moves into the starting lineup.

 Walter Clayton Jr. (ankle) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Clayton, who played 23 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics, is dealing with a sprained right ankle. However, the probable tag suggests that he’s more likely to play on Wednesday than not. The Mavericks will have Kyrie Irving, and his availability limits Clayton’s ceiling, even if he remains in the rotation.

 Max Christie (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Christie, who missed Dallas’ last two games, fully participated in Tuesday’s practice. If he can play on Wednesday, that may push Marcus Sasser out of the rotation after he logged 18 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.

 Kyrie Irving (knee) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Irving is back after sitting out Sunday’s loss to the Celtics. His return bumps Naji Marshall to the bench after he made a spot start the last time out. 
 Kyrie Irving 
 DAL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Kyrie Irving (knee) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Irving, who played 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers, played both games of Dallas’ most recent back-to-back on November 8-9. After playing 29 minutes in a win over the Nets, he played 39 minutes the following night against the Pacers. If Irving can’t play on Sunday, Walter Clayton Jr. will get more minutes, and Marcus Sasser could enter the rotation. 
 Kyrie Irving 
 DAL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Kyrie Irving amassed a team-high 34 points (11-of-25 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block over 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers. 
 Irving was one of the few bright spots for Dallas in this one as they struggled to get anything going offensively until it was too late. The veteran point guard knocked down 7-of-16 from three-point range and fell just one point shy of matching his previous season-high, which he set earlier this week against the Pacers. He’s delivered second-round fantasy value this season, averaging 22.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.4 assists, 1.3 steals and 0.5 blocks through 11 games. The Mavericks are back in action with a quick turnaround when they face the Celtics, another one of Irving’s former teams, on Sunday. 
 Kyrie Irving 
 DAL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Kyrie Irving matched a season-high with 35 points (11-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs) and four assists over 38 minutes in Monday’s win over the Pacers. 
 It was a two-man show for Dallas in this one with Irving and Cooper Flagg combining for an eye-popping 78 of their 125 points. The pair hoisted 43 shot attempts total and connected on 10-of-16 three-pointers. Seven of those conversions from long range came courtesy of Irving as he put together one of his best shooting efforts in recent memory, matching his previous season-high mark in the scoring department set against the Rockets back on October 30. The 34-year-old point guard is putting together an impressive campaign, averaging 22.9 points, 3.2 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.2 steals through nine games.

 Kyrie Irving tallied 21 points (9-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Nets. 
 Irving played 29 minutes on Sunday, sitting the entire fourth quarter because Dallas held a large lead. The Mavericks guard has scored at least 21 points in four of his eight appearances this season and continues to strengthen his chemistry with Cooper Flagg. Unfortunately for those rostering Irving, Week 4 could be tough. The Mavericks host the Pacers on Monday, then play another back-to-back on Saturday and Sunday. Irving managers may not get more than two games of production.

 Darius Garland accumulated 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
 While Garland kept the turnovers in check, committing one, and recorded a full stat line, he had a tough night shooting the basketball. The Clippers guard was 5-of-15 from the field, a far cry from his 50.6 percent shooting for the season. The biggest concern for him in fantasy basketball has been the turnovers, so there’s no need to lose sleep over Garland having an off shooting night.

 Rui Hachimura amassed 20 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
 After scoring 24 points on 7-of-24 shooting in his previous three games, Hachimura needed a night like Tuesday, even if the Clippers were on the wrong end of a blowout. This was Hachimura’s second game this season with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Even better for fantasy managers was his 70 percent shooting from the field, a strong output for a player shooting 41.5 percent on the season.

 Keyonte George tallied 30 points (10-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, 11 assists, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Clippers.
 While Brice Sensabaugh recorded his first 40-point double-double in Tuesday’s victory, George recorded his first 30-point double-double. The Jazz point guard is shooting 43.4 percent from the field this season, and a night like Tuesday will certainly help with that number. Also, George committed just two turnovers, the fewest in a game for him in the last four games. George missed the first game of Utah’s most recent back-to-back, so it isn’t guaranteed that he’ll play on Wednesday against the Lakers after playing 35 minutes on Tuesday.

 Brice Sensabaugh shot 16-of-21 from the field in Tuesday’s win over the Clippers, scoring 40 points with 11 rebounds, five assists, one block and eight three-pointers.
 While the eight three-pointers were a career high for Sensabaugh, this wasn’t his first rodeo as a 40-point scorer. The Jazz forward has three 40-point games in his NBA career, but this was his first 40-point double-double. Add in the five assists, and this was a great night for the few who are rostering Sensabaugh. Utah visits the Lakers on Wednesday and plays three more games this week.

 Jrue Holiday accounted for 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 With Deni Avdija ruled out, the Trail Blazers needed someone to step up offensively. Holiday was still used in a reserve role, but his 19 shot attempts tied him with Damian Lillard for the most on the team. Jrue finished with a full line, and he’s become a bit more valuable to fantasy managers since Ja Morant strained his hamstring. Jayson Kent started for Avdija, finishing with eight points, three rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers.

 Damian Lillard finished Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
 Lillard finished with 25 points, but his layup attempt in the final seconds, which would have given Portland the win, was blocked by Minnesota’s Trey Lyles. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of the 10 games Portland has played since losing Ja Morant to a hamstring injury, providing top-100 fantasy value. Portland visits Milwaukee on Thursday in Lillard’s first game against the Bucks since being waived in the summer of 2025.

 After recording at least five assists in five straight games, Ball had two in the Timberwolves’ two games against Portland. Ball finished Tuesday’s win one rebound shy of a double-double, offering unexpected value in that category. Even with the recent low assist numbers, field-goal percentage and turnovers remain Ball’s biggest issues in category leagues.
